title: No Pod activation possible since Android 16 Update
body:
Did the Pixel Android 16 Update Yesterday. 
Connection to Dash wored fine so far.
Today i tried a Pod change. 
Deactivating old Dash worked fine.
But there is no Activation for New Pod possibe

Bonding Mode didn't work too

What are possibilitiea to check?

comments.body:
Adding my findings. 

My phone is a Pixel 7 Pro. Running Android 15 until today with no issues on the Dash pods. I was never using the Dash bond setting.

Today I updated to Android 16, and the current pod continued to work with no settings change in AAPS.

Then I deactivated the current pod and tried to activate a new pod. The pod fails to activate with the following error:  "Failed to connect to pod"

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/466797e2-4f4a-4020-9fee-8da4acd12a51)

The logcat shows the following:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/000be122-a991-45a1-8f80-37a69b8d3c91)

It fails waiting for the connection here:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ec5eba5-c57d-4754-915b-22e2647f1e0d)

This is so weird, because the same function call is used for active pods, so why was it working earlier in the day for me, but now is failing with a new pod? I also tried bonding the pod manually in the android settings and it still fails to connect.

I tried with nrf app to bond. It connects and bonds. Then tried to activate the pod in AAPS and it fails the same way. nRF log here:
[Log 2025-06-11 17_12_35.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20698794/Log.2025-06-11.17_12_35.txt)

Finally, I activated my pod on my backup device. It's a pixel 2, but that doesn't matter. I then saved the settings file from the backup phone and imported into my main phone. Now the main phone is able to connect to the pod and issue commands no problems. It's been running fine for the last 2 hours this way.

Trying to experiment with your main diabetes phone is foolish thing... And upgrading to unsupported system is very foolish thing... There have been a lot of reports of different drivers/pumps not working with Android 15, and you go and upgrade to system (Android 16), that is even less supported...

@olorinmaia Thanks a lot for the instructions. The cherry-pick worked for me. But only after I’d navigated the state space into a whole new level of confusion: `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Trying to set Bluetooth Address to 40:EE:BE:64:C5:67, but it is already set to 40:EE:BE:68:34:29`. Oddly enough, this happened both _with_ and _without_ the fix during connection attempts. The root cause was rather dumb:

0. I filled a pod after an Android 16 upgrade. The connection failed, alternating between _“Could not find an available pod for activation”_ and _“Failed to connect to pod”_.
0. I had recently had a couple of pod failures (2 out of 30 were faulty — no beeps when filled, no activation).  They only ever produced the first error, **not** the second one. Despite knowing that, I jumped to a wrong conclusion: a faulty pod.
0. Then I filled another pod, paid close attention whether it beeped as expected, etc. Then the error messages started to alternate between 3 variations, including the one (far) above.
0. I found and applied this fix, which reduced the number of random error messages down to the `java.lang.IllegalStateException` one. Some progress there, but I still didn’t have a working pod.
0. Ultimately I ended up tossing a coin and killing one of the two filled pods. Not sure if it mattered which one it was. In any case, it worked and initialized a pod after that.

Just mentioning this for the record, in case someone encounters the same kind of confusing situation.

EDIT: Eventually I did manage to activate a pod, but it was quite nerve-wracking:

0. Noticed that both _Activate_ and _Deactivate_ buttons were enabled.
0. Went outside Bluetooth range, pressed _Deactivate_, waited until Bluetooth connection expired, then pressed the button that forgets the pod. (The goal was to not _actually_ deactivate the pod.)
0. Walked back to the pod, tried to activate it. Got _Could not find an available pod for activation_ this time instead of _Failed to connect to pod_.
   * At that point I almost thought the pod was already one state machine step too far, never to be reconciled with AndroidAPS…
0. Yet after 5+ more attempts, the pod has been successfully activated.
